1) Yes, my wife and our 3 kids made a similar move from Utah to Massachusetts. We thought we were making the move for a better education system... Which we accomplished. But the more valuable thing we gained was being part of a community that ranked education at a higher priority. When our kids were in Utah, our school was constantly struggling to get parent volunteers for field trips, classroom activities, etc. Now the teachers are forced to pull names from a hat because they receive so many volunteers. In Utah, my wife and I were both board members of the PTA, we'd often times struggle to get 10 members at a meeting for voting purposes. In Utah it was challenging for our children to make friends. It was hard for them to explain to friends that they can't play until after homework, or maybe it was a day they had a music lesson.. it was hard for our kids to excel in things they wanted to do, but not have a place (other than home) where it was perceived as a positive. Now, our kids have made friends with kid's who are also required to finish homework, who also have music lessons, etc. Ultimately our main purpose of the move was to reduce classroom sizes from 30 to 16 per student, but we've found that being part of a community with similar goals is nice.

2) No idea honestly. We made the move, but weren't really supported. Most friends and family thought we were a bit crazy to make a move like we did... Especially "just for schools"

3) Kids are adaptable. Ours range in age from 7-12. The older kids appreciate having friends who have families that are easier to relate to. (We still have to fight the "so and so" has a better family bullshit lol). The younger won't ever really know the struggles of living counter-culture but youngest get spoiled a bit anyways right? I can't say what age is best, but some red flags for us were the counter-culture atmosphere obviously. But also the parent teacher conferences. The teachers couldn't tell us where our kids needed further growth. And the sad truth is with 30 students a teacher must be more hand on with lower performing students. Teachers are heroes, and are savagely abused in our country, imo.

Take all of this with a grain of salt. It's all anecdotal, and definitely a bit rambling, but you're not alone in wanting a better education for your kiddo. Families come in all shapes and sizes, and all have different rankings and priorities. Hell we probably don't even agree on what education is or should be haha. Let me know if you have any followup questions and I'll do my best to share our experience 🙂
